# Regenerate

Prompt

I need to extract the data from this chart. Can you help?

![Original Chart](1982_McMillan_etal_figure3.png)

Response

The following table was returned.

| Hypocotyl-Plumule Elongation (mm) | \% of Seedlings |
|-----------------------------------|-----------------|
| 0                                 | 38%             |
| 1-5                               | 22%             |
| 6-10                              | 18%             |
| 11-15                             | 13%             |
| 16-20                             | 4%              |
| 21-25                             | 2%              |
| 26-30                             | 2%              |

Prompt

Can you put the data into a CSV format?

Response

Hypocotyl-Plumule Elongation (mm),% of Seedlings 0,38 1-5,22 6-10,18 11-15,13 16-20,4 21-25,2 26-30,2

Prompt

Can you make the R code to create a bar chart with these data?

Response

```{r}
# Load required library
library(ggplot2)

# Create the data frame
data <- data.frame(
  elongation = c("0", "1-5", "6-10", "11-15", "16-20", "21-25", "26-30"),
  percentage = c(38, 22, 18, 13, 4, 2, 2)
)

# Create the bar chart
ggplot(data, aes(x = elongation, y = percentage)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", fill = "skyblue", color = "black") +
  labs(title = "Hypocotyl-Plumule Elongation in Seedlings",
       x = "Hypocotyl-Plumule Elongation (mm)",
       y = "% of Seedlings") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
```

Prompt

The order of the bars isn't correct. They should be in ascending order, left to right.

Note

This is the common problem of needing the categories to be factors. It's one of the "R things" that confuses a lot of beginners.

Response

```{r}
# Load required library
library(ggplot2)

# Create the data frame
data <- data.frame(
  elongation = c("0", "1-5", "6-10", "11-15", "16-20", "21-25", "26-30"),
  percentage = c(38, 22, 18, 13, 4, 2, 2)
)

# Convert elongation to a factor with levels in the correct order
data$elongation <- factor(data$elongation, levels = c("0", "1-5", "6-10", "11-15", "16-20", "21-25", "26-30"))

# Create the bar chart
ggplot(data, aes(x = elongation, y = percentage)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", fill = "skyblue", color = "black") +
  labs(title = "Hypocotyl-Plumule Elongation in Seedlings",
       x = "Hypocotyl-Plumule Elongation (mm)",
       y = "% of Seedlings") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
```

Note

The chart is basically correct. The next stages ask for style modifications.

Prompt

Can you modify the code so the third bar is orange?

Response

```{r}
# Load required library
library(ggplot2)

# Create the data frame
data <- data.frame(
  elongation = c("0", "1-5", "6-10", "11-15", "16-20", "21-25", "26-30"),
  percentage = c(38, 22, 18, 13, 4, 2, 2)
)

# Convert elongation to a factor with levels in the correct order
data$elongation <- factor(data$elongation, levels = c("0", "1-5", "6-10", "11-15", "16-20", "21-25", "26-30"))

# Create a color vector
bar_colors <- c("skyblue", "skyblue", "orange", rep("skyblue", 4))

# Create the bar chart
ggplot(data, aes(x = elongation, y = percentage, fill = elongation)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", color = "black") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = bar_colors) +
  labs(title = "Hypocotyl-Plumule Elongation in Seedlings",
       x = "Hypocotyl-Plumule Elongation (mm)",
       y = "% of Seedlings") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
        legend.position = "none")  # Remove the legend
```

Note

This worked just right. More modifications to the style are then requested.

Prompt

I'd like you to remove the grid lines and make the value labels on both axes in black and slightly larger.

```{r}
# Load required library
library(ggplot2)

# Create the data frame
data <- data.frame(
  elongation = c("0", "1-5", "6-10", "11-15", "16-20", "21-25", "26-30"),
  percentage = c(38, 22, 18, 13, 4, 2, 2)
)

# Convert elongation to a factor with levels in the correct order
data$elongation <- factor(data$elongation, levels = c("0", "1-5", "6-10", "11-15", "16-20", "21-25", "26-30"))

# Create a color vector
bar_colors <- c("skyblue", "skyblue", "orange", rep("skyblue", 4))

# Create the bar chart
ggplot(data, aes(x = elongation, y = percentage, fill = elongation)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", color = "black") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = bar_colors) +
  labs(title = "Hypocotyl-Plumule Elongation in Seedlings",
       x = "Hypocotyl-Plumule Elongation (mm)",
       y = "% of Seedlings") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.text = element_text(color = "black", size = 12),
    axis.title = element_text(color = "black", size = 14),
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    legend.position = "none"
  )
```

Note

This, too, worked as expected. But there seems to be a need for y-axis tick marks.

Prompt

I need tick marks on the y axis.

Response

```{r}
# Load required library
library(ggplot2)

# Create the data frame
data <- data.frame(
  elongation = c("0", "1-5", "6-10", "11-15", "16-20", "21-25", "26-30"),
  percentage = c(38, 22, 18, 13, 4, 2, 2)
)

# Convert elongation to a factor with levels in the correct order
data$elongation <- factor(data$elongation, levels = c("0", "1-5", "6-10", "11-15", "16-20", "21-25", "26-30"))

# Create a color vector
bar_colors <- c("skyblue", "skyblue", "orange", rep("skyblue", 4))

# Create the bar chart
ggplot(data, aes(x = elongation, y = percentage, fill = elongation)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", color = "black") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = bar_colors) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 40, by = 10), limits = c(0, 40)) +
  labs(title = "Hypocotyl-Plumule Elongation in Seedlings",
       x = "Hypocotyl-Plumule Elongation (mm)",
       y = "% of Seedlings") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.text = element_text(color = "black", size = 12),
    axis.title = element_text(color = "black", size = 14),
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_line(color = "gray", size = 0.5),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    axis.ticks.y = element_line(color = "black"),
    axis.line.y = element_line(color = "black"),
    legend.position = "none"
  )
```

Note

There was a note about the use of a depreciated statement. Basically, use *linewidth* instead of *size*.

Horizontal grid lines were added as well as the ticks, but that's OK.
